recent_articles.rephrased_article: **UDF** is expected to form a Cabinet in the coming week, with high chances of representation for six districts in north Kerala.  The **Congress**, **IUML**, and two Independents secured 21 candidates each from Kasaragod, Wayanad, Kannur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, and Palakkad districts. Several prominent figures within the **Congress** and other parties are potential nominees for ministerial positions, including **Sunny Joseph**, **K.K. Shailaja**, and **A.P. Anil Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: PM to visit Bengaluru on May 10 to address 45th anniversary of Art of Living; BJP to offer reception at HAL Airport - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** will visit Bengaluru on May 10 to attend the 45th anniversary celebrations of **The Art of Living** and the 70th birthday of its founder, **Sri Sri Ravi Shankar**. The BJP State unit is preparing a reception for the Prime Minister upon his arrival at HAL Airport.  He will deliver a speech at a public event followed by an address at the Art of Living International Centre campus where he will inaugurate new facilities and participate in various programs including a meditation session for World Peace led by **Sri Sri Ravi Shankar**.

recent_articles.title: Women voters rejected Congress, allies for opposing Reservation Bill, says Nandyal MP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Byreddy Shabari**, **TDP national general secretary**, stated that women voters have rejected the Congress, DMK, and Trinamool Congress for opposing the Women’s Reservation Bill.  Shabari claimed these parties were responsible for the bill's defeat in Parliament and that women voters delivered a "fitting lesson" by defeating them in recent elections. She expressed confidence that the NDA government will pass the bill soon and implement the 33% reservation for women.

recent_articles.title: What happens if a Chief Minister refuses to relinquish office after electoral defeat? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, **Mamata Banerjee**, chairperson of the **Trinamool Congress**, refused to resign as Chief Minister, claiming the results were a result of a conspiracy.  She stated that the election was not conducted fairly and accused the BJP of misusing central forces. However, legal experts suggest that an election petition can be filed challenging the results based on allegations of voter deletion during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal. The tenure of the current Assembly ends on May 7, at which point a new government will be formed.

recent_articles.title: Telangana CM Revanth directs police to minimise public inconvenience during VIP movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **A. Revanth Reddy**, Chief Minister of **Telangana**, directed the **DGP C.V. Anand** to ensure smooth traffic flow during convoy movements and the movement of other dignitaries across the state.  Following a traffic congestion incident near the airport, Reddy instructed officials to avoid prolonged road waits due to convoy arrangements and stressed action against responsible personnel. The DGP convened a video conference with police officers from various commissionerates, emphasizing the need for streamlined traffic regulation and the establishment of a dedicated Traffic Bureau.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka’s deep tech programme ELEVATE NxT draws strong response from startups across India - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The first cohort of **ELEVATE NxT**, a national grant-in-aid program for deep tech startups by the **Department of Electronics, IT, and Bt in Karnataka**, has received applications from across India.  Of the 983 total applications, 213 are from outside Karnataka, representing nearly 23% of the total. The selected candidates will pitch to a jury on May 6, 2026, with the final cohort selection following a three-week process. **Priyank Kharge**, IT-Bt Minister of Karnataka, announced this program in January 2026 as part of the state's "Deep Tech Decade" initiative.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Congress-led UDF won not due to any individual’s efforts but as people were fed up, says NSS general secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Sukumaran Nair**, general secretary of the **Nair Service Society (NSS)**, stated that the Congress-led UDF's victory in the 2026 Kerala Assembly polls was due to public dissatisfaction with the government and not individual efforts by anyone, including **V.D. Satheesan**.  **Mr. Nair** attributed the Left's loss to internal issues within the party, not anti-incumbency sentiment. While acknowledging differences with **Satheesan**, he emphasized that these were not used against him during the election and asserted that the NSS did not dictate support for any candidate.
